heading.en: What the forehead trial found, result by result

title.en: Forehead roughness fell 7.4% in 20 days while it rose 4.3% on placebo

body.en: The Skin Visioscan VC98 photographs the skin's surface with a built-in camera and calculates its roughness from the image. The figure here is cR2, a maximum-roughness value that the paper describes as indicative of fine lines. Each woman was measured seated in an armchair with her eyes closed and her face at rest, after 20 minutes in a room held at 19 to 21 °C, so the lines were imaged in the same relaxed state every time.

On the Argireline® cream, the group's average cR2 went from 83.8 at the start to 77.6 at day 20, a fall of 7.4%. On the placebo cream it went from 82.3 to 85.8, a rise of 4.3%. The paper reports that difference as significant (P = .022; Tables 2 and 3, Figure 1). The Argireline® group's average kept edging down afterwards, to 75.0 at day 40.

For a reader, this is forehead skin measurably smoother within three weeks of twice-daily use, read by a camera rather than judged by eye. The authors note that the forehead is where cosmetics aimed at moderate lines are usually measured, and it is where this trial's clearest results were ([Raikou et al., 2017](https://doi.org/10.1111/jocd.12314)).

title.en: Water loss through the skin fell by days 20 and 40 while it rose on placebo

body.en: A Tewameter TM300 measures how fast water evaporates from the skin. Its probe is an open cylinder held against the skin, with humidity and temperature sensors at two heights; the difference between them gives the rate of water loss. The lower the reading, the more of its moisture the skin is holding on to.

On the Argireline® cream, the group's average reading went from 8.1 at the start to 5.7 at day 20 and 5.4 at day 40. On the placebo cream it went from 7.0 to 10.0 and then 18.0. The paper reports both gaps as significant: P = .025 at day 20 and P = .01 at day 40 (Table 2, Figure 3).

Argireline® was the only one of the trial's four creams under which water loss fell, and dryness was reported only in the placebo group. For a reader, that is skin that held on to more of its moisture through the first 40 days of use ([Raikou et al., 2017](https://doi.org/10.1111/jocd.12314)).

No person, no skin, no water droplets or 'hydration' imagery (the register forbids a 'hydrates' claim), no logo or text. Suggested filename: skingenetix-argireline-skin-water-loss-probe-study.jpg.

heading.en: How does Argireline® affect forehead skin?

mechanisms._why_none: ZERO blocks proposed. Raikou tested no mechanism: the authors write that 'the possible mechanisms of the influence of acetyl hexapeptide-3 ... on skin barrier have not been defined in our study' and that there is 'no evidence in the bibliography regarding the correlation of the tested peptides with TEWL'. The water-loss finding is therefore a result (outcome 2), not a mechanism. The only laboratory finding specific to Argireline (SNARE complex, Blanes-Mira 2002) is used on the Wang 2013 page; a second, reworded copy here would be the same block. The section draws nothing while items is empty.
